segments.en:
Parashas Aikev links hearing the mitzvos with humility, yirah, remembering Hashem’s kindnesses, and recognizing that all strength and abundance come from Him. The manna, Bircas HaMazon, Eretz Yisrael, love of the convert, and Vehayah im shamoa become a path toward nullifying pride, deveikus, and a life of emunah.

Hearing → humility and yirah → remembering Hashem’s kindnesses → nullifying “my strength and the power of my hand” → blessing and deveikus → Eretz Yisrael and life

And so it is. Blessed is He who watches over us with perfect care, and there is no peeling off until He is cleansed from our sins. But the wicked and the wicked disbelievers do not trust in the care of Hashem. Blessed is He with perfect care, for they do not blink the eyes of their knowledge of Hashem.

segments.en: “Only to fear.” There are people who fall very deeply in their own eyes, and because of this they rebel even more. They imagine that they are already so far away that there is no hope, as if fear of Hashem no longer applies in their place. Against this the prophet cries out and rebukes: even the sea has a boundary of sand that it cannot pass; so too a person must know that fear of Hashem reaches him even there.

segments.en:
Only to Fear (Deuteronomy 10:12)

For if the sons of men are afraid of the knowledge that they have fallen too far, and because of this they are rebellious and rebellious, then it will be allowed. And all this from a heat that seems to them that they have become so far removed from it that there is no hope, and as if a grave were allowed to them, mercy and peace, mercy and peace, as if in their place there is no longer fear from there, then it will be blessed. And because This is what the prophet Mochicha cries out and says (Jeremiah 5:1): "My people will not fear, and so on, and so on, for the waters are a limitless river that I have set, which they have not seen, and they will not cross over." The water is even the most powerful, and the shells of the last straw are strong.

segments.en: This is like the teaching of the Sages: today the evil inclination tells him to do this, and tomorrow to do that. After a person turns away from the good path, he may not remind himself to return immediately, but instead goes farther each time. Because of his fall he rebels more, until he can leave the boundary completely. Therefore the verse says that they did not say in their heart, “Let us now fear Hashem.”

segments.en: This is the test of what our late rabbis said: "Today it is said to him, 'Do this and that.'" And this is what the prophet concluded: "But this was a rebellious heart and a teacher turned away and went away. And if they had not said in their hearts, 'We fear Hashem,'" "Turn away and go away," it would have been better, because after they turned away from the path of goodness and tzaddikness, it was not enough that they did not remember themselves. To return from the hand, even they went to Hell, and there was a remnant at every turn, because from the heat of their fall they were still stubborn and rebellious, until they were able to go out from the border to the very end. segments.en: Now, Israel, what does Hashem your God require of you? For if our ancestors were afraid and hardened, and if they were afraid of a young man, it was not for Moses' sake to be afraid of a young man. And the matter is puzzling: For what did they profit by their eagerness to run after Moses' sake to be afraid of a young man, even harder than what Hashem said, "Hashem will require of you," and so on. Fear of Hashem, my Lord, is our refuge, and what will benefit us? What is their refuge? Is Hashem my refuge? Will not Hashem my refuge protect us? Is Hashem my refuge? This verse also indicates the light of the will, which is in the sight of God, in the sight of God, Hashem your God, ask of me.

And the greater the understanding, the more the light of the will, which is the gift of fear (as is explained elsewhere), every man can easily attain, because the will is eternal, it only needs to be strong. In the examination of a soldier, etc., this depends on this, because there is no reinforcer, etc., but from where is the beginning, is it possible to achieve? segments.en: Therefore Moshe says, “And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you?” “Now” specifically: after all the toil I endured for you, taking you from Egypt, giving you the Torah with awesome signs, and illuminating you with holy knowledge. Even after all this, when there were failures and descents, the service remains to begin now, from this moment.

This awakens him to pray always, to say Tehillim and many supplications, and to beg Hashem to have true compassion on him and draw him to the true leader, until he leaves the spirit of folly. Especially he should increase hisbodedus, private speech and prayer between himself and his Creator.

segments.en: Later, when you examine what is your great goodness, you will be strengthened, therefore you must always strengthen yourself at all times with a strong desire for Hashem. You will be blessed from every place that is, because by this your body will be awakened and strengthened constantly. And you will be blessed abundantly by saying many praises and supplications and petitions, that Hashem, whose true mercy is upon him, may have mercy on him and touch you. Blessed is the true guide who is in the midst of the trial, 'for he will guide them with compassion.' Until he is granted the right to depart from the spirit of foolishness, etc. And in detail to increase in solitude, which is conversation and prayer between us and our Lord, until his heart is poured out like water.

When they unite together in the unity of the Oneness, they realize that they are the Ones who have attained all the worlds. segments.en: “So that your days may increase.” The main rectification of honor, which is the aspect of malchus, is through tzedakah; through this, tzedek is made into tzedakah. Therefore the main intention in building a home should be to bring worthy poor people into it and to make it a gathering place for sages, as the Sages taught: “Let your house be open wide,” “let the poor be members of your household,” and “let your house be a meeting place for the sages.” Through this, honor is complete, and the house becomes a holy house.

segments.en: “Without righteousness… he makes his fellow work for nothing” describes the brazen-faced who rule over the poor for nothing. This is the aspect of the name Shaddai written on the mezuzah, for this name is the aspect of the tzaddik, and of tzedakah: “the tzaddik is gracious and gives.” Through tzedakah, honor is lifted away from the brazen-faced and returned to those who understand true knowledge. Then honor has a holy face, and this is the main rectification of the holy home through the mitzvah of mezuzah.
